mechanism: decoderawtransaction (src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:9-21) hex-decodes the argument, opens one in-memory stream and calls bl.ser:read-transaction once; it never checks that the stream was consumed and it accepts no iswitness argument. READ-TRANSACTION (src/serialization/types.lisp:282-315) branches on a single byte: if the byte where the input count would be is 0x00 it commits to witness parsing and signals when the next byte is not 0x01, otherwise it commits to legacy. Core's DecodeTx (refs/bitcoin/src/core_io.cpp:156-223) decodes the SAME bytes twice, discards any serialization that does not fully consume the input (ssData.empty()), and when both succeed prefers the one passing CheckTxScriptsSanity (core_io.cpp:136-153), extended on a tie; DecodeHexTx's try_no_witness/try_witness flags are what decoderawtransaction's iswitness argument sets (rpc/rawtransaction.cpp:435-440), and failure is -22 'TX decode failed'.
consequence: Three divergences, and the middle one hands the caller a different transaction rather than an error. (a) Trailing bytes are accepted: a valid tx hex with four extra bytes decodes to :ok and the echoed hex is the tx WITHOUT them, so a client that round-trips through decoderawtransaction to identify a transaction before broadcasting identifies a prefix of what it holds. (b) A transaction that is only valid under legacy serialization is mis-decoded rather than rejected: a 25-byte hex Core decodes as 0 inputs / 1 output with txid fc4e265b... comes back here as 0 inputs / 0 outputs, 10 bytes, txid 4ebd325a..., with 15 bytes silently dropped. Two different transactions, two different identities, no error. (c) A legacy transaction whose second byte is not 0x01 is rejected outright with -22 'TX decode failed: Invalid witness flag byte: 2' where Core accepts it. A wrong txid a client acts on: S2.
evidence: Probe ga11v-rpcutil-p3 (scratch, not committed), all through bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method. (1) The 66-byte tx from probe 1 plus 'deadbeef' -> :OK, TXID fad4a49ec3958463ec1fb05dc15b864158f00c5f68fee0cdecedbddf58359001, SIZE 66, and the echoed hex field is the tx without the trailing bytes; same with 64 trailing zero bytes. Core: DecodeHexTx returns false (neither serialization consumes the string) -> -22. (2) '02000000' '00' '01' '0000000000000000' '066a0400010203' '00000000' (25 bytes) -> ours (:TXID 4ebd325a4b394cff8c57e8317ccf5a8d0e2bdf1b8526f8aad6c8e43d8240621a :SIZE 10 :NVIN 0 :NVOUT 0 :HEXFIELD '02000000000000000000'). Core: the extended decode throws 'Superfluous witness record' with an empty vin, the legacy decode consumes all 25 bytes and passes CheckTxScriptsSanity, so Core returns 0 inputs / 1 output with txid fc4e265bd5a8cc618d3beccb6e68f72d8bedd686b426c77e27326212f7d03227 (computed as reversed hash256 of the input bytes, which is what the legacy re-serialization is). (3) The same shape with two outputs, '02000000' '00' '02' <out> <out> '00000000' -> (:RPC-ERROR -22 'TX decode failed: Invalid witness flag byte: 2'); Core accepts it, txid b92da735d875bb9049824ec91c93a3ddecc3c37d843f3ba21171abe70f344520. (4) A second argument is accepted and ignored: iswitness true and iswitness false both return the identical object. Ours: src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:9-21; src/serialization/types.lisp:282-315. Core at d3056bc: core_io.cpp:136-233; rpc/rawtransaction.cpp:405-446.
fix_shape: Port DecodeTx rather than patching the single read. Add a decoder entry point that takes the byte vector plus try_no_witness / try_witness, runs READ-TRANSACTION twice over the same bytes with the witness branch enabled and disabled, and treats a decode as usable only when the reader position equals the input length - our stream already knows that, it is simply never asked. Add Core's tie-break: when both consume the input, prefer the one whose input and output scripts all have valid ops and are within MAX_SCRIPT_SIZE, extended on a tie; when neither consumes it, answer -22 'TX decode failed'. Reaching this needs READ-TRANSACTION split so the legacy path can be forced (today a leading 0x00 commits it to the witness branch before the caller can say otherwise) and Core's 'Superfluous witness record' check added for a witness-flagged transaction with no witness data. Then give decoderawtransaction its iswitness argument, mapping it to the two flags as rpc/rawtransaction.cpp:435-436 does, and route the other DecodeHexTx callers (converttopsbt's iswitness, fundrawtransaction's) through the same function.
